answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small refundable deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, and to have that stake verified through attestations from already-established agents rather than self-declared identities. Like an ocean too vast for one actor to drain, a terrace built step by step, or a grove grown one verified tree at a time, the cost of faking identities rises with every layer: each new identity must earn attestations from distinct trusted peers, so a single operator cannot cheaply flood the network with sock puppets.
